first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent this, so I read it properly. It's a flowers article, which is really her department, but the opening is sensible rather than gushing. "The piece that stops you scrolling was styled for one room, one table shape and one light." Fair point. I'll keep going to see whether it gets to the practical side and the money.

journey.quote: Ask the venue about open flame, set-up and pack-down before you fall for a design.
journey.reaction: Good. That's the question I'd be asking, and it's right up the top instead of buried.

journey.quote: Guests need to see and speak to the person opposite.
journey.reaction: Yes. My mother is hard of hearing and hates talking through a hedge of flowers. Sensible.

journey.quote: Move ceremony arrangements to the reception rather than buying twice.
journey.reaction: Now we're talking. Spending sensibly. I'd underline this one for my husband.

journey.quote: Stems are the expensive part of most arrangements, so the levers are about using fewer of them well:
journey.reaction: Helpful, but no idea of what anything costs. I understand it links elsewhere for that. Not a problem for this article.

journey.quote: Each idea below is a starting point to adapt to your palette.
journey.reaction: Thirty is a lot for me. The short 'Suits' line under each one makes it easy to skim on the iPad, so I don't mind. This is my daughter's bit anyway.

journey.quote: A candle is an open flame that can easily ignite combustible items nearby, so keep dried grasses, paper menus and trailing greenery well clear of it.
journey.reaction: Thank you. Someone is thinking about safety, not just photos. With elderly relatives at the table, I want candles in glass.

journey.quote: Heavily scented blooms such as lilies, tuberose and some jasmine can compete with the meal and bother sensitive guests.
journey.reaction: Very practical. My sister gets headaches from lilies. This is the kind of detail I trust.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, so these details are settled before anything is booked.
journey.reaction: In writing, before anything is booked. That's the line I'd forward to my husband.

journey.quote: Can you work from our mood board and send a sample photo before the day?
journey.reaction: Good list of questions, and I like having it written down. But it never asks the florist the money questions: what's the deposit, is the quote in writing, what currency. That's what I'd want to know before my daughter pays someone she's never met.

journey.quote: When can the florist access the room to set up, and when must everything be cleared?
journey.reaction: Fine, but who do we actually ring on the day if the flowers turn up wrong? The venue questions don't ask who the contact person is.

journey.section: Planning the table with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, start to finish.
journey.reaction: One person, and they handle payments too. That reassures me more than anything about candles. I'd still want to speak to them on the phone first.

unanswered_questions: If an overseas florist takes a deposit and doesn't deliver, who is responsible, and is the money protected?
Will quotes from overseas florists come in AUD or in local currency, and in English?
Who do we ring on the wedding day if the flowers or set-up go wrong, given the time difference?
Can I speak to the Wedded Advisor on the phone before anything is booked?
Does the Wedded Advisor help with older or less mobile guests, for example seating them away from candles or near the exit?
would_share_with: My husband, with the 'in writing before anything is booked' line and the 'buying twice' tip highlighted
My daughter, to say keep the flowers low so Nana can hear, and keep the lilies off the tables

cta_reaction.quote: Begin the conversation with our Wedded Concierge team.
cta_reaction.why: I wouldn't enquire because of a centrepiece article, but the 'one Wedded Advisor ... payments ... start to finish' line is what I'd want. I'd want to know I can have a phone call with a real person. I'd likely leave the enquiry to my daughter and ask to be on the call.

top_3_changes: Add written-quote and deposit questions to the florist checklist (questions only, no claims). Old: "- Who handles pack-down, and do you take back hired items?" New: "- Who handles pack-down, and do you take back hired items?\n- Can you put the quote, what is included and the timings in writing?\n- What deposit do you need, and when is the balance due?"

Add an on-the-day contact question to the venue checklist. Old: "- When can the florist access the room to set up, and when must everything be cleared?" New: "- When can the florist access the room to set up, and when must everything be cleared?\n- Who is our contact on the day if something needs changing?"
Nothing else would stop me. The tone is plain and sensible, the paragraphs are short, and the 'in writing before anything is booked' line is the strongest thing on the page. Leave it where it is.

checks.check: every point has an exact quote from the draft
stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent)
no invented brand facts; missing information listed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments ignored
suggested edits stay within brand limits: no fees, commissions, sourcing or vetting claims, no new facts or measurements; exact old/new strings given

open_questions.question: Deposit protection, currency and phone contact are unanswered. For a styling post, treat them as nice-to-have, or send them to CRO for the CTA block? The suggested checklist edits are questions for suppliers only and make no brand claims.

assumptions: Persona is provisional and uncalibrated, so reactions reflect the card only.
Read on an iPad from a link her daughter sent, so she read the whole post carefully, top to bottom.
